#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Creates a new directory inside the directory created by the previous run.
#
# Usage:
#   ./create_nested_dir.sh [root_directory]
#
# First run:
#   creates: root_directory/<new-dir>
# Later runs:
#   creates: root_directory/<new-dir>/<new-dir>/...
#
# The latest created directory is tracked in .nested_dir_last by default.
# Override with: NESTED_DIR_STATE=/path/to/state ./create_nested_dir.sh

root_dir="${1:-nested_dirs}"
state_file="${NESTED_DIR_STATE:-.nested_dir_last}"

if [[ -f "$state_file" ]]; then
  previous_dir="$(<"$state_file")"
else
  previous_dir="$root_dir"
fi

# If the tracked previous directory was deleted, start again from the root.
if [[ ! -d "$previous_dir" ]]; then
  previous_dir="$root_dir"
fi

mkdir -p "$previous_dir"

base_name="dir_$(date -u +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
new_dir="$previous_dir/$base_name"

# Avoid collisions if the script is run more than once in the same second.
if [[ -e "$new_dir" ]]; then
  suffix=1
  while [[ -e "${new_dir}_$suffix" ]]; do
    suffix=$((suffix + 1))
  done
  new_dir="${new_dir}_$suffix"
fi

mkdir "$new_dir"
printf '%s\n' "$new_dir" > "$state_file"

echo "Created: $new_dir"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Creates a new directory inside the directory created by the previous iteration,
# continuing indefinitely with a while loop.
#
# Usage:
#   ./create_nested_dir.sh [root_directory] [delay_seconds]
#
# Example:
#   ./create_nested_dir.sh nested_dirs 1
#
# The latest created directory is tracked in .nested_dir_last by default.
# Override with: NESTED_DIR_STATE=/path/to/state ./create_nested_dir.sh
#
# Stop with Ctrl+C.

root_dir="${1:-nested_dirs}"
delay_seconds="${2:-1}"
state_file="${NESTED_DIR_STATE:-.nested_dir_last}"

if [[ -f "$state_file" ]]; then
  previous_dir="$(<"$state_file")"
else
  previous_dir="$root_dir"
fi

# If the tracked previous directory was deleted, start again from the root.
if [[ ! -d "$previous_dir" ]]; then
  previous_dir="$root_dir"
fi

mkdir -p "$previous_dir"

echo "Creating nested directories under: $root_dir"
echo "Delay between creations: ${delay_seconds}s"
echo "Stop with Ctrl+C."

while true; do
  base_name="dir_$(date -u +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
  new_dir="$previous_dir/$base_name"

  # Avoid collisions if the loop runs more than once in the same second.
  if [[ -e "$new_dir" ]]; then
    suffix=1
    while [[ -e "${new_dir}_$suffix" ]]; do
      suffix=$((suffix + 1))
    done
    new_dir="${new_dir}_$suffix"
  fi

  mkdir "$new_dir"
  printf '%s\n' "$new_dir" > "$state_file"

  echo "Created: $new_dir"
  previous_dir="$new_dir"

  sleep "$delay_seconds"
done

content.text: Tiny issue from the test: with sub-second delays, timestamp names can repeat at different nesting levels. That’s valid, but ugly. I’m switching the loop to a simple counter so names are clearer and unique.

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Creates a new directory inside the directory created by the previous iteration,
# continuing indefinitely with a while loop.
#
# Usage:
#   ./create_nested_dir.sh [root_directory] [delay_seconds]
#
# Example:
#   ./create_nested_dir.sh nested_dirs 1
#
# The latest created directory is tracked in .nested_dir_last by default.
# Override with: NESTED_DIR_STATE=/path/to/state ./create_nested_dir.sh
#
# Stop with Ctrl+C.

root_dir="${1:-nested_dirs}"
delay_seconds="${2:-1}"
state_file="${NESTED_DIR_STATE:-.nested_dir_last}"

if [[ -f "$state_file" ]]; then
  previous_dir="$(<"$state_file")"
else
  previous_dir="$root_dir"
fi

# If the tracked previous directory was deleted, start again from the root.
if [[ ! -d "$previous_dir" ]]; then
  previous_dir="$root_dir"
fi

mkdir -p "$previous_dir"

counter=1

echo "Creating nested directories under: $root_dir"
echo "Delay between creations: ${delay_seconds}s"
echo "Stop with Ctrl+C."

while true; do
  new_dir="$previous_dir/dir_$counter"

  # Avoid collisions if resuming in a directory that already has numbered children.
  while [[ -e "$new_dir" ]]; do
    counter=$((counter + 1))
    new_dir="$previous_dir/dir_$counter"
  done

  mkdir "$new_dir"
  printf '%s\n' "$new_dir" > "$state_file"

  echo "Created: $new_dir"
  previous_dir="$new_dir"
  counter=$((counter + 1))

  sleep "$delay_seconds"
done

Or with a custom root and delay:


It will create:

```text
nested_dirs/dir_1
```
